name: ClickHouse Operator
summary: A Kubernetes operator that observes ClickHouseInstallation and ClickHouseKeeperInstallation resources, reconciles StatefulSet-based clusters, and coordinates lifecycle changes through status and worker tasks.

features.name: Custom-resource desired state
features.description: The operator uses ClickHouseInstallation and related custom resources as declarative inputs for cluster, host, configuration, storage, and lifecycle settings.
benefits: Makes database topology and configuration inspectable through Kubernetes APIs
Allows users to express changes without directly managing every generated workload
costs: CRD schema and compatibility constrain the operator contract
Desired state remains separate from the readiness of generated resources

features.name: Hierarchical reconciliation workers
features.description: Reconciliation decomposes an installation into cluster, shard, and host work, with controller and worker code applying changes and updating status across generated Kubernetes resources.
benefits: Separates topology-level decisions from host-level operations
Supports incremental retries and status reporting for long-running changes
costs: Partial progress and retries create intermediate states
Ordering across workers and Kubernetes resources affects convergence

features.name: Stateful storage and database lifecycle
features.description: The operator materializes ClickHouse hosts as StatefulSet-backed pods with persistent volumes and coordinates version, scaling, replication, backup, and recovery settings through reconciliation.
benefits: Preserves stable pod identity and persistent storage for database hosts
Centralizes operational lifecycle policy in the custom-resource model
costs: Database changes are constrained by StatefulSet and storage semantics
Scaling, rolling changes, and backups require coordination with live data state

mathematical_views.question: How does a custom-resource specification and observed Kubernetes state drive repeated actions toward a ClickHouse installation target?
assumptions: The CRD specification is the desired state
Generated resources and statuses provide observations
Actions are sufficiently idempotent for retries

mathematical_views.question: How can installation, cluster, shard, and host transitions be composed while preserving ordering and status invariants?
assumptions: A failed child transition can prevent parent completion
The model abstracts Kubernetes controller scheduling

mathematical_views.question: Which mapping between database hosts, StatefulSet pods, persistent volumes, and cluster roles is preserved across rescheduling or controlled scale changes?
assumptions: StatefulSet identity and volume claims remain stable under supported operations
Cluster topology names identify the intended host roles
The view abstracts ClickHouse internal replication protocol

costs: CRD evolution and generated-resource drift add coordination overhead
Eventual convergence and partial failure complicate diagnosis

benefits: Stable storage identity for stateful database hosts
costs: Safe scale, upgrade, and backup operations require workload-aware sequencing
